definition_zh: 疏忽；过失；失职；过失侵权
definition_en: a failure to exercise the care that a reasonable person or a competent professional should exercise
core_image: 本该伸手扶住，却把手缩了回去
scene: 仓库的叉车通道没有画线，新来的工人被撞伤了脚。The injured worker sued the warehouse for negligence in failing to mark the forklift lane.
sceneCN: 这里的 negligence 是「过失」（第 1 个义项：未尽合理注意的疏忽）；句意：受伤的工人以仓库未划出叉车通道的过失为由提出索赔。

pos.zh: 疏忽；过失；失职；（法律）过失责任

forms.label: 无变化（不可数名词，无复数）

derivatives.zh: 由 negligence 去掉名词后缀 -ence、换成形容词后缀 -ent，义为「疏忽的；过失的」
由 negligent 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「疏忽地」
与 negligence 同出拉丁语 neglegere，义为「忽视；疏于照管」
由拉丁词干加 -ible 构成，义为「微不足道的；可忽略的」

senses.title: Ordinary carelessness
senses.definition: a lack of the care an ordinary person would take in doing something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事时缺少常人应有的谨慎
senses.example: The keys were lost through his own negligence.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙是因为他自己的疏忽才丢的。
senses.why: The Latin verb neglegere means to disregard, literally not to pick something up, so negligence is care that was never taken up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 neglegere 意为「不理、不顾」，字面是「不去拾起」，所以过失就是本该拾起的照料始终没有被拾起。

senses.title: Breach of a duty of care
senses.definition: in law, a failure to meet the standard of care owed to another that causes recoverable harm
senses.definitionCN: 法律上未达到对他人应负的注意标准，并造成可获赔偿的损害
senses.example: The court held the hospital liable for negligence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定医院应对过失承担责任。
senses.why: Once the law recognises a duty of care, careless conduct stops being merely unfortunate and becomes a civil wrong.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律承认注意义务的存在，粗心行为就不再只是运气不好，而成为一种可诉的民事不法，这正是日常疏忽长成法律概念的关键一步。

senses.title: Professional negligence
senses.definition: the failure of a professional to reach the standard expected of a competent member of that profession
senses.definitionCN: 专业人士未达到该行业合格从业者应有的水准
senses.example: The solicitor was accused of professional negligence over the missed filing date.
senses.exampleCN: 这名律师因错过提交日期被指职业过失。
senses.why: Where skill is promised, the measure of care rises from the ordinary person to the competent practitioner.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人以专业技艺提供服务时，注意的尺度就从普通人提高到合格从业者，同一种疏忽因此有了更高的门槛。

senses.title: Contributory negligence
senses.definition: the careless conduct of the claimant that helps cause the harm and reduces the damages awarded
senses.definitionCN: 索赔人自身的疏忽行为促成了损害，因而减少可获得的赔偿
senses.example: Her damages were reduced by thirty per cent for contributory negligence.
senses.exampleCN: 由于共同过失，她的赔偿金被削减了三成。
senses.why: Fault can be shared: the same careless thread runs through both parties, so the loss is divided instead of being laid at one door.
senses.whyCN: 过错可以由双方分担：同一根粗心的线穿过两边，损失便按比例分开，而不是全部算在一方头上。

senses.title: Gross negligence
senses.definition: a serious departure from the care required, more blameworthy than ordinary negligence and close to recklessness
senses.definitionCN: 严重偏离应有的注意，比一般过失更应受责难，接近轻率
senses.example: The carrier could not rely on the exemption clause because of gross negligence.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存在重大过失，承运人不能援引免责条款。
senses.why: Courts grade carelessness by degree, and the worst degree earns a harsher label and weaker legal protection.
senses.whyCN: 法院按程度给疏忽分级，最重的一级会得到更严厉的标签和更弱的免责保护，这是核心意象在程度上的延伸。

senses.title: Criminal negligence
senses.definition: carelessness grave enough for the criminal law to treat it as the fault element of an offence
senses.definitionCN: 严重到足以被刑法视为犯罪过错要件的疏忽
senses.example: The site manager was charged with criminal negligence after the collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 坍塌事故后，工地经理被控刑事过失。
senses.why: When careless conduct kills or endangers life, the state may turn the civil failure of care into a crime.
senses.whyCN: 当粗心行为致人死亡或危及生命时，国家会把民事上的未尽注意转化为刑事罪名，同一个疏忽因此跨进了刑法领域。

intro.en: Negligence comes from Latin neglegentia, carelessness, from neglegere, to disregard.
intro.cn: negligence 来自拉丁语 neglegentia（疏忽），源于 neglegere（不理、忽视）。

items.en: Legere means to pick up, gather, or read, and the prefix neg- denies it.
items.cn: legere 意为拾起、收集或阅读，前缀 neg- 把它否定。

items.en: Neglegere therefore means not to pick something up, hence to disregard it.
items.cn: neglegere 因此意为「不去拾起」，引申为「不予理会」。

items.en: Neglegentia, the noun of carelessness, is formed from the participle stem of the verb.
items.cn: 表示疏忽的名词 neglegentia 由该动词的分词词干构成。

items.en: Old French negligence keeps the Latin sense of carelessness.
items.cn: 古法语 negligence 保留了拉丁语「疏忽」的含义。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century as a general term for carelessness.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，用作泛指疏忽的词。

items.en: Modern legal usage narrows it into a breach of the duty of care.
items.cn: 现代法律用法把它收窄为违反注意义务。

note.en: Negligence sits in the family of neglegere, beside neglect, negligent, and negligible, and near the wider vocabulary of fault.
note.cn: negligence 属于 neglegere 词族，与 neglect、negligent、negligible 相邻，也靠近表示过错的更大词场。

entries.definition: to fail to look after or attend to something
entries.definitionCN: 忽视；疏于照管（与 negligence 同出 neglegere）

entries.definition: showing a lack of proper care
entries.definitionCN: 疏忽的；过失的（由 negligence 换后缀而来的形容词）

entries.definition: so small or slight as to be unimportant
entries.definitionCN: 微不足道的；可忽略的（同出 neglegere，但意义已经偏移）

entries.definition: the quality of not being careful
entries.definitionCN: 粗心；不谨慎（日常近义词，不带法律含义）

entries.definition: careless action taken without regard to an obvious risk
entries.definitionCN: 轻率；不顾明显风险的鲁莽（程度重于 negligence）

entries.definition: a lack of strictness or care in supervision
entries.definitionCN: 松懈；监管不严（多指管理上的疏忽）

normalIntro.en: Negligence is care that was never picked up: neg- says no, legere says to gather, and the hand stays open.
normalIntro.cn: negligence 是始终没有被拾起的照料：neg- 表示「不」，legere 表示「拾起」，而那只手一直松着。

normal.en: Neg- means not and legere means to pick up, so to neglect a duty is literally not to pick it up.
normal.cn: neg- 表示「不」，legere 表示「拾起」，所以 neglect a duty 字面上就是「不去拾起义务」。

normal.en: The family runs negligence, negligent, negligently, and neglect.
normal.cn: 这个词族依次是 negligence、negligent、negligently 与 neglect。

normal.en: Learn the legal trio: duty of care, breach, and damage.
normal.cn: 记住法律上的三件套：注意义务、违反义务、损害后果。

normal.en: Gross negligence is worse than ordinary negligence, while contributory negligence is the share of the claimant.
normal.cn: 重大过失重于一般过失，共同过失则是索赔人自己那一份过错。

normal.en: Compare neglect: neglect is the act of leaving something unattended, while negligence names the quality or the legal wrong.
normal.cn: 对比 neglect：neglect 指把某事搁下不管的行为，negligence 则指这种品性或法律上的过失。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that opens just as a rope should be gripped.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在该握紧绳子的时候忽然松开。

abstract.en: Picture a driver looking down at a phone while a child steps off the kerb.
abstract.cn: 想象司机低头看手机，而一个孩子正走下路缘。

abstract.en: Picture a surgeon ignoring a checklist pinned beside the operating table.
abstract.cn: 想象外科医生无视贴在手术台旁的核对清单。

examples.en: The loss was caused by the negligence of the warehouse.
examples.cn: 损失是由仓库的疏忽造成的。

examples.en: The claim rests on negligence, not on breach of contract.
examples.cn: 这项索赔依据的是过失，而不是违约。

examples.en: Gross negligence may strip a party of its contractual protection.
examples.cn: 重大过失可能使一方失去合同保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼格利真丝」——尼格把一卷真丝随手搁在门口，任人踩来踩去，事后只说一句忘了收。

root: 拉丁语 neg-（不）+ legere（拾起、理会）→ neglegere（不去理会）→ neglegentia（疏忽）→ 古法语 negligence → 英语 negligence，核心义「该拾起的照料没有拾起」。

sensesIntro.en: Negligence starts as everyday carelessness, becomes a legal breach of duty, and is then graded by setting, by share of fault, and by seriousness.
sensesIntro.cn: negligence 从日常的粗心开始，转为法律上的违反注意义务，再按场景、过错份额与严重程度分级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opening instead of holding on.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该握紧的手却松开了。

branches.en: Everyday carelessness is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 日常的粗心是本义。

branches.en: A recognised duty turns carelessness into a legal wrong.
branches.cn: 被承认的注意义务把粗心变成法律上的不法。

branches.en: A professional standard raises the measure of care.
branches.cn: 职业标准抬高了注意的尺度。

branches.en: Shared fault and criminal fault show the same failure seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 分担过错与刑事过错是同一疏忽从两个方向看到的样子。

branches.en: Gross negligence marks the top of the scale before recklessness.
branches.cn: 重大过失标出轻率之前的最高一级。

intro.en: Negligence is built from the Latin neg- and legere, and English has grown a whole family around it.
intro.cn: negligence 由拉丁语 neg- 与 legere 构成，英语围绕它长出了整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin neglegere means to disregard, and its noun neglegentia means carelessness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neglegere 意为「不理」，其名词 neglegentia 意为「疏忽」。

items.example: The prefix neg- denies the act of picking up.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 neg- 否定了「拾起」这个动作。

items.example: Legere gives the image of taking something up.
items.exampleCN: legere 提供「把东西拾起来」的意象。

items.example: Neglegere joins the prefix to the verb.
items.exampleCN: neglegere 把前缀与动词合在一起。

items.example: Neglegentia is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: neglegentia 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Negligence keeps both the everyday and the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: negligence 同时保留日常与法律两种含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ence forms negligence from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 让拉丁词干构成 negligence。

items.example: Negligent adds the adjectival suffix -ent.
items.exampleCN: negligent 加了形容词后缀 -ent。

items.meaningCN: 具有某种性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ent turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Negligently adds the adverb suffix -ly.
items.exampleCN: negligently 加了副词后缀 -ly。

items.example: Neglect is the shorter verb from the same source.
items.exampleCN: neglect 是同源而来的较短动词。

items.example: Negligible shows how far the family can drift in meaning.
items.exampleCN: negligible 显示这个词族的意义可以漂移多远。

definition_zh: 侵权行为；民事不法行为
definition_en: a civil wrong, independent of contract, that causes harm for which the injured party may sue
core_image: 一条笔直的界线被扭弯，越过去便压坏了邻人的花圃
scene: 货车的尾板没有扣好，转弯时甩出去砸坏了路边店铺的橱窗。The shopkeeper brought a claim in tort against the haulage company.
sceneCN: 这里的 tort 是「侵权行为」（第 1 个义项：造成他人损害的民事不法行为）；句意：店主以侵权为由向运输公司提出索赔。

pos.zh: 侵权行为；民事不法行为；（法律）侵权

derivatives.zh: 由 tort 加形容词后缀 -ious，义为「侵权行为的；构成侵权的」
由 tort 与表示「做者」的 feasor 合成，义为「侵权行为人」
由 tortious 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「以侵权方式地」

senses.title: The civil wrong
senses.definition: a wrongful act that causes harm and is not a breach of contract, giving the injured party a right to sue
senses.definitionCN: 造成他人损害、且不属于违约的民事不法行为，受害方因此有权起诉
senses.example: A claim in tort is separate from a claim under the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 侵权索赔与依合同提出的索赔是两回事。
senses.why: The Latin tortum means something twisted or wrong, so a tort is conduct that has been turned away from the lawful path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tortum 意为「被扭歪的、不正的」，所以侵权行为就是把本该走正的行为扭到一边，这正是核心意象的法律化。

senses.title: A single act of injury
senses.definition: one particular wrongful act of this kind, such as damaging the property of another person
senses.definitionCN: 此类不法行为中的某一起，例如损坏他人的财物
senses.example: The spill was a tort that polluted the neighbouring land.
senses.exampleCN: 这次泄漏是一起污染邻人土地的侵权行为。
senses.why: The category counted one act at a time becomes a countable event that a court can examine.
senses.whyCN: 把这个类别按单次行为来数，它就变成法院可以逐案审理的具体事件。

senses.title: Intentional tort
senses.definition: a tort committed on purpose, such as assault, battery, or trespass
senses.definitionCN: 故意实施的侵权行为，例如威胁、殴打或侵入他人土地
senses.example: Battery is an intentional tort.
senses.exampleCN: 殴打属于故意侵权。
senses.why: The twisted act can be deliberate, and the law marks purpose as a distinct branch of tort.
senses.whyCN: 被扭歪的行为可以是有意为之，法律便把「故意」标为侵权的一个独立分支。

senses.title: Negligence as a tort
senses.definition: a tort that arises from carelessness rather than from a deliberate act
senses.definitionCN: 由疏忽而非故意行为引起的侵权
senses.example: Most road accident claims are negligent torts.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数交通事故索赔都属于过失侵权。
senses.why: The same twisted outcome can come from a hand that simply failed to hold, so carelessness forms its own branch.
senses.whyCN: 同样的扭歪结果也可以出自一只没有握稳的手，于是疏忽自成一支，与故意侵权并列。

senses.title: Strict liability tort
senses.definition: a tort for which the defendant is liable without proof of fault, as with dangerous animals or defective products
senses.definitionCN: 无须证明过错即可令被告承担责任的侵权，例如危险动物或缺陷产品致害
senses.example: Keeping a dangerous animal can create a strict liability tort.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养危险动物可能构成严格责任侵权。
senses.why: Some activities are so risky that the law stops asking about care and attaches liability to the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 有些活动风险太高，法律便不再追问是否小心，而把责任直接附着在活动本身，这是核心意象在风险领域的延伸。

senses.title: Tort law as a field
senses.definition: the branch of civil law that deals with such wrongs and their remedies
senses.definitionCN: 处理此类不法行为及其救济的民法学分支
senses.example: She teaches tort alongside contract and property.
senses.exampleCN: 她和合同法、财产法一起教授侵权法。
senses.why: Once the single wrongs are gathered together, they form a whole field of law with its own rules and remedies.
senses.whyCN: 当一起起不法行为被归拢起来，它们就构成一个拥有自身规则与救济手段的完整法律领域。

intro.en: Tort comes from Latin tortum, a wrong, from tortus, the past participle of torquere, to twist.
intro.cn: tort 来自拉丁语 tortum（不法、侵害），源于 torquere（扭、拧）的过去分词 tortus。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or turn, and its participle tortus means twisted.
items.cn: torquere 意为扭、拧或转动，其分词 tortus 意为「被扭歪的」。

items.en: Tortum, literally something twisted, comes to mean a wrong or an injustice.
items.cn: tortum 字面是「被扭歪之物」，引申为不法或不公。

items.en: Medieval Latin keeps tortum as the name of a wrong.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留 tortum 作为「不法行为」的名称。

items.en: Old French tort means wrong or injury.
items.cn: 古法语 tort 意为不法和侵害。

items.en: English borrows tort through Anglo-French as a general word for wrong.
items.cn: 英语经由盎格鲁法语借入 tort，泛指不法与侵害。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word is used for a class of civil wrongs distinct from contract.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，该词被用来指与违约相区别的一类民事不法行为。

note.en: Tort belongs to the twisted family of torquere, alongside tortious and tortuous, and to the vocabulary of civil wrongs and remedies.
note.cn: tort 属于 torquere 这个「扭」的词族，与 tortious、tortuous 同源，也靠近民事不法与救济的词汇场。

entries.definition: of or relating to a tort
entries.definitionCN: 侵权行为的（由 tort 派生的形容词，勿与 tortuous 混淆）

entries.definition: full of twists and turns, not straightforward
entries.definitionCN: 曲折的；迂回的（同出 torquere，但与侵权无关）

entries.definition: a person who commits a tort
entries.definitionCN: 侵权行为人（由 tort 与 feasor 合成的法律术语）

entries.definition: an act that is unjust or unlawful
entries.definitionCN: 不法行为；冤屈（比 tort 更宽泛的日常词）

entries.definition: a civil wrong in Scots and civil law
entries.definitionCN: 不法行为（苏格兰法与大陆法中与侵权对应的术语）

entries.definition: harm done to a person or to a right
entries.definitionCN: 损害；伤害（侵权成立所要求的后果，而不是行为本身）

normalIntro.en: A tort is a twist: torquere turns a lawful path aside, and the law names the injury that follows.
normalIntro.cn: tort 是一次扭折：torquere 把正当的路扭向一边，法律便给随之而来的损害命名。

normal.en: Torquere means to twist, tortus means twisted, and a tort is conduct twisted away from what is lawful.
normal.cn: torquere 意为扭，tortus 意为被扭歪的，tort 则是被扭离正路的行为。

normal.en: Keep tortious and tortuous apart: tortious belongs to tort, while tortuous means winding.
normal.cn: 把 tortious 与 tortuous 分开：前者属于侵权，后者意为曲折。

normal.en: Collocations: tort law, tort claim, tort liability, intentional tort.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：侵权法、侵权索赔、侵权责任、故意侵权。

normal.en: Contrast contract: contract is a broken promise, tort is a broken duty fixed by law.
normal.cn: 对比 contract：合同是违背承诺，侵权是违反法律固定的义务。

normal.en: A tortfeasor is the person who commits the tort.
normal.cn: tortfeasor 就是实施侵权行为的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary line bent out of shape until it crosses the garden of a neighbour.
abstract.cn: 想象一条地界被扭弯，越进了邻家的花园。

abstract.en: Picture a leaking tank left beside a field, its oil creeping into the soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只漏油的罐子放在田边，油慢慢渗进土里。

abstract.en: Picture a lit match held to the fence of a neighbour on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象有人故意把点着的火柴凑到邻家的篱笆上。

examples.en: The claim in tort seeks damages for the damaged wall.
examples.cn: 这项侵权索赔要求赔偿受损的围墙。

examples.en: Intentional torts require proof of intent, while negligent torts do not.
examples.cn: 故意侵权需要证明故意，过失侵权则不需要。

examples.en: Tort law protects interests that the parties never agreed to protect by contract.
examples.cn: 侵权法保护当事人从未在合同中约定保护的利益。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托特」——托特倒车时把邻家的篱笆顶歪，还怪风向不对，邻人只好告他侵权。

root: 拉丁语 torquere（扭、拧）→ 过去分词 tortus（被扭歪的）→ 中性名词 tortum（不法、侵害）→ 古法语 tort → 英语 tort，核心义「被扭离正路的行为」。

sensesIntro.en: Tort moves from the general category of civil wrong to a single instance, then to the main types, and finally to the field of law.
sensesIntro.cn: tort 从民事不法的总称，走到单起行为，再分出主要类型，最后成为一个法律部门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight boundary twisted until it crosses the ground of a neighbour.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔直的界线被扭弯，越进邻人的地界。

branches.en: The broad category of civil wrong is the core sense.
branches.cn: 民事不法的总称是核心义项。

branches.en: One instance of injury is the countable use.
branches.cn: 单起损害事件是可数用法。

branches.en: Intentional torts are the deliberate branch.
branches.cn: 故意侵权是有意为之的一支。

branches.en: Negligent torts are the careless branch.
branches.cn: 过失侵权是粗心大意的一支。

branches.en: Strict liability and the field of tort law complete the map.
branches.cn: 严格责任与侵权法这个领域补全了整张图。

intro.en: Tort is a Latin twisting noun, and English has tortious, tortfeasor, and the wider torquere family around it.
intro.cn: tort 是拉丁语中表示「扭」的名词，英语围绕它有 tortious、tortfeasor 以及更大的 torquere 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin torquere means to twist, and tortum names the twisted thing, hence a wrong.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭，tortum 指被扭歪之物，因此也指不法。

items.example: Torquere supplies the twisting image behind tort.
items.exampleCN: torquere 提供 tort 背后「扭」的意象。

items.example: Tortus is the past participle of the verb.
items.exampleCN: tortus 是该动词的过去分词。

items.example: Tortum is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: tortum 是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.example: Tort narrows the old wrong into a legal category.
items.exampleCN: tort 把古老的「不法」收窄为一个法律类别。

items.example: Tortious adds the adjectival suffix -ious.
items.exampleCN: tortious 加了形容词后缀 -ious。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ious forms tortious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ious 构成 tortious。

items.example: Tortfeasor joins tort to an old French agent word.
items.exampleCN: tortfeasor 把 tort 与一个古法语施动词结合起来。

items.example: Tortuous keeps the literal twisting sense.
items.exampleCN: tortuous 保留了字面的「扭」义。

items.example: Distort adds the prefix dis- to torquere.
items.exampleCN: distort 在 torquere 前加了前缀 dis-。

items.meaning: to twist something out of a person
items.example: Extort adds the prefix ex- to the same root.
items.exampleCN: extort 在同一词根前加了前缀 ex-。

items.example: Contort adds the prefix con- to the same root.
items.exampleCN: contort 在同一词根前加了前缀 con-。

definition_en: a process in which a neutral third party helps disputing parties reach a voluntary agreement
core_image: 一位长者隔着一道矮墙，替两户人家来回传话
scene: 两家供货商为一批迟到的货物争执不下，谁也不肯先让步。A neutral adviser brought both suppliers into mediation and helped them sign a settlement.
sceneCN: 这里的 mediation 是「调解」（第 1 个义项：由中立第三方协助当事人协商并达成协议的过程）；句意：一位中立顾问把两家供货商引入调解，帮他们签下和解协议。

derivatives.zh: 由 mediate 加表示施动者的后缀 -or，义为「调解人；斡旋者」
由拉丁语 mediare 而来，义为「调解；居中斡旋」
由 mediator 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「调解的；斡旋的」

senses.title: Assisted negotiation
senses.definition: a process in which a neutral person helps the parties to a dispute talk and reach their own agreement
senses.definitionCN: 由中立者协助争议双方对话并自行达成协议的过程
senses.example: Mediation is often faster and cheaper than litigation.
senses.exampleCN: 调解往往比诉讼更快、更便宜。
senses.why: The word comes from medius, the middle, so mediation places a neutral person in the middle of two sides.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 medius（中间的），所以调解就是把一个中立者放到两方之间，核心意象正是「站在中间」。

senses.title: A single mediation
senses.titleCN: 一次调解；一起调解案件
senses.definition: one particular session or case in which this process is used
senses.definitionCN: 运用这一过程的某一次会谈或某一宗案件
senses.example: The parties settled at their second mediation.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在第二次调解时达成了和解。
senses.why: The same process, counted as an event with a date and a place, becomes a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 同一套过程一旦有了时间地点、可以被数出来，就成了可数名词，这是核心动作被「事件化」的结果。

senses.title: Mediation inside the court system
senses.titleCN: 法院附设调解；诉前调解
senses.definition: mediation encouraged or ordered by a court, often before trial, whose settlement may become a court order
senses.definitionCN: 由法院鼓励或指令进行的调解，通常在审判之前，其和解结果可以转为法院命令
senses.example: The judge stayed the case and sent the parties to court-annexed mediation.
senses.exampleCN: 法官中止了案件，把双方送去法院附设调解。
senses.why: When courts route cases to a mediator, the middle position gains a procedural slot before the trial.
senses.whyCN: 当法院把案件分流给调解人时，「中间位置」就在审判之前获得了一个程序上的位置。

senses.title: Mediation between states
senses.definition: mediation in which a neutral state, envoy, or organisation helps governments settle a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 由中立国家、特使或国际组织协助政府之间解决争端的调解
senses.example: A regional envoy led the mediation between the two governments.
senses.exampleCN: 一位区域特使主持了两国政府之间的调解。
senses.why: The middle position scales up: a neutral envoy stands between states instead of individuals.
senses.whyCN: 「中间位置」可以放大：站在中间的不再是个人，而是国家之间的中立特使。

senses.title: Mediation as a profession
senses.definition: the professional practice of acting as a mediator, with its own training, standards, and fees
senses.definitionCN: 以担任调解人为职业的实践，有自己的培训、规范与收费
senses.example: She trained in mediation before leaving private practice.
senses.exampleCN: 她在离开私人执业之前接受过调解培训。
senses.why: Repeated practice turns the activity into a recognised profession with its own standards.
senses.whyCN: 反复从事同一种活动，会使它变成一门有自身规范的职业，这是核心动作在社会分工中的延伸。

intro.en: Mediation comes from Medieval Latin mediatio, from mediare, to be in the middle, from medius, middle.
intro.cn: mediation 来自中世纪拉丁语 mediatio，源于 mediare（居于中间），再往上溯是 medius（中间的）。

items.en: Medius means middle, the point between two ends.
items.cn: medius 意为中间的，即两端之间的位置。

items.en: Mediare means to be in the middle or to halve, and it yields the agent noun mediator.
items.cn: mediare 意为居于中间或对半分，并由此产生施动名词 mediator。

items.en: Mediatio names the act of coming between parties.
items.cn: mediatio 指走到各方之间进行调停的行为。

items.en: Old French mediation carries the sense of intervening to reconcile.
items.cn: 古法语 mediation 带有介入促和的含义。

items.en: English adopts mediation in the fifteenth century for the act of interceding.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 mediation，用来指居中斡旋的行为。

items.en: Modern usage ties the word to structured and voluntary dispute resolution outside the courts.
items.cn: 现代用法把该词与法院之外有结构、自愿参与的争议解决方式联系起来。

note.en: Mediation stands in the middle of the medius family, next to mediate and mediator, and beside the other ways of settling disputes.
note.cn: mediation 站在 medius 词族的中间，与 mediate、mediator 相邻，也与其它解决争议的方式并列。

entries.definition: to act as a go-between in a dispute
entries.definitionCN: 调解；居中斡旋（mediation 的动词形式）

entries.definition: a neutral person who conducts a mediation
entries.definitionCN: 调解人；斡旋者（加 -or 表示施动者）

entries.definition: direct, with nothing in between
entries.definitionCN: 直接的；立即的（同出 medius，前缀 in- 表示「没有中间环节」）

entries.definition: dispute resolution in which a third party imposes a binding award
entries.definitionCN: 仲裁（第三方作出有约束力的裁决，与调解的关键区别在此）

entries.definition: a process in which a third party helps the parties reconcile
entries.definitionCN: 和解；调解（更强调促使双方和好，程序常更宽松）

entries.definition: direct bargaining between the parties without a third party
entries.definitionCN: 谈判；协商（双方直接谈，没有中立第三方）

normalIntro.en: Mediation places a middle person between two sides: medius is the middle, and the mediator carries words across it.
normalIntro.cn: mediation 把一个处在中间的人放到两方之间：medius 是中间，调解人则在中间来回传话。

normal.en: Medius means middle, and mediation puts a neutral person in the middle of a dispute.
normal.cn: medius 意为中间，mediation 则把中立者放进争议的中间。

normal.en: The family runs mediate, mediator, mediation, and mediatory.
normal.cn: 这个词族依次是 mediate、mediator、mediation 与 mediatory。

normal.en: Collocations: mediation process, mediation agreement, court-annexed mediation.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：调解程序、调解协议、法院附设调解。

normal.en: Compare arbitration: a mediator helps the parties decide, while an arbitrator decides for them.
normal.cn: 对比 arbitration：调解人帮当事人自己作决定，仲裁人替他们作决定。

normal.en: A settlement reached in mediation is voluntary, which is both its strength and its limit.
normal.cn: 调解达成的和解是自愿的，这既是它的长处，也是它的限度。

abstract.en: Picture an elder standing at a low wall, passing words from one household to the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一位长者站在矮墙边，把话从一户人家传到另一户。

abstract.en: Picture the same two sides returning for a second session, calmer than at the first.
abstract.cn: 想象同一对当事人第二次坐到一起，比第一次平静许多。

abstract.en: Picture a judge stepping back from the bench and pointing the parties to a side room.
abstract.cn: 想象法官从审判席上退一步，把双方指向旁边的一间调解室。

examples.en: The parties chose mediation instead of a trial.
examples.cn: 双方选择调解而不是审判。

examples.en: A mediation agreement is enforceable once it is signed.
examples.cn: 调解协议一经签署即具有执行力。

examples.en: The court encouraged mediation before the case went to trial.
examples.cn: 法院在案件进入审判前鼓励双方调解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「梅迪埃申」——梅迪站在两家人中间，左一句右一句来回递话，最后两家握手言和。

root: 拉丁语 medius（中间的）→ mediare（居于中间、居中）→ 中世纪拉丁语 mediatio（居中调停）→ 古法语 mediation → 英语 mediation，核心义「站在中间传话」。

sensesIntro.en: Mediation names the assisted process, then a single session, then the court-connected and interstate versions, and finally the profession itself.
sensesIntro.cn: mediation 先指受协助的协商过程，再指单次会谈，然后是法院附设与国际两种场景，最后指这门职业本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a neutral person standing in the middle, passing words between two sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个中立的人站在中间，把话在两方之间传递。

branches.en: The assisted process is the core sense.
branches.cn: 受协助的协商过程是核心义项。

branches.en: A single session is the countable use.
branches.cn: 单次会谈是可数用法。

branches.en: Court-annexed mediation adds a procedural setting.
branches.cn: 法院附设调解增加了程序场景。

branches.en: International mediation scales the same middle position up to states.
branches.cn: 国际调解把同一个「中间位置」放大到国家层面。

branches.en: A session and the profession show the practice as event and as career.
branches.cn: 单次会谈与职业化实践，是同一件事作为事件与作为职业的两种样子。

intro.en: Mediation is built on Latin medius, middle, and English has mediate, mediator, and immediate around it.
intro.cn: mediation 建立在拉丁语 medius（中间）之上，英语围绕它有 mediate、mediator 与 immediate。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius means middle; mediare means to be in the middle, and mediatio names the act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medius 意为中间；mediare 意为居于中间，mediatio 则指这一行为。

items.example: Medius supplies the middle position of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: medius 提供整个词族的「中间」位置。

items.meaning: to be in the middle, to halve
items.example: Mediare turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: mediare 把形容词变成动作。

items.example: Mediatio is the direct source of mediation.
items.exampleCN: mediatio 是 mediation 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -or marks the person who acts.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 标出实施动作的人。

items.example: Mediation keeps the procedural sense of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: mediation 保留了拉丁名词的程序含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion forms mediation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 mediation。

items.example: Mediate is the verb behind mediation.
items.exampleCN: mediate 是 mediation 背后的动词。

items.example: Mediator adds the agent suffix -or.
items.exampleCN: mediator 加了施动后缀 -or。

items.meaningCN: 表示施动者的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -or forms mediator and tortfeasor alike.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 既能构成 mediator，也能构成 tortfeasor。

items.example: Mediatory adds the adjectival suffix -y.
items.exampleCN: mediatory 加了形容词后缀 -y。

items.meaningCN: 直接的；中间没有环节的
items.example: Immediate denies the middle with the prefix in-.
items.exampleCN: immediate 用前缀 in- 否定了「中间」。

items.example: Medium keeps the literal middle sense.
items.exampleCN: medium 保留了字面的「中间」含义。

definition_en: a written law enacted by a legislature or by another body with law-making power
core_image: 一块刻满条款的石板立在广场中央，人人都要照着它行事
scene: 市议会通过一项新条例，规定所有商店夜里必须关灯。The new statute requires every shop to switch off its lights after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里的 statute 是「成文法」（第 1 个义项：立法机关制定的成文法律）；句意：这项新法规要求所有商店午夜之后关灯。

pos.zh: 成文法；法规；法令；（机构）章程

derivatives.zh: 由 statute 加形容词后缀 -ory，义为「法定的；成文法规定的」
由 statutory 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「依法定地」
由 statute 与 barred 合成的法律形容词，义为「受法定时效限制的」

senses.title: An enacted written law
senses.definition: a written law formally enacted by a parliament, a congress, or a similar legislative body
senses.definitionCN: 由议会、国会或类似立法机关正式制定的成文法律
senses.example: The statute bans the sale of single-use plastics.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法规禁止销售一次性塑料制品。
senses.why: The Latin statutum is something set up and fixed, so a statute is a rule that has been stood upright and made binding.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 statutum 意为被立起、被固定之物，所以成文法就是一条被立直并赋予约束力的规则。

senses.title: The instrument itself
senses.titleCN: 一部成文法律；法案文本
senses.definition: the enacted instrument as a document, cited by its title, sections, and date
senses.definitionCN: 作为文件存在的法律文本，按名称、条款与日期被引用
senses.example: Section five of the statute defines the offence.
senses.exampleCN: 该法第五条界定了这一罪名。
senses.why: Once a rule is fixed in writing, lawyers deal with the document itself, citing sections and dates.
senses.whyCN: 规则一旦被固定在文字里，法律人面对的就是这份文件本身，按条款与日期引用，这是「石板」意象的文本化。

senses.title: Law made by legislation
senses.definition: the part of a legal system that consists of enacted laws rather than judicial decisions
senses.definitionCN: 法律体系中由立法制定的法律构成的部分，与司法判决相对
senses.example: Statute law now covers most of the field once left to the common law.
senses.exampleCN: 制定法如今覆盖了过去多由普通法处理的领域。
senses.why: Counting the individual acts together gives a whole source of law, set against case law.
senses.whyCN: 把一部部法律合起来数，就得到与判例法相对的一整个法律渊源，这是从单块石板到整面墙的扩展。

senses.title: The limitation statute
senses.titleCN: 诉讼时效法规；法定时效
senses.definition: the statutory period within which a claim must be brought, often called the statute in practice
senses.definitionCN: 必须提出索赔的法定期间，实务中常直接称作 the statute
senses.example: The claim is barred because the statute has run.
senses.exampleCN: 由于法定时效已过，这项索赔已不能成立。
senses.why: Practice shortens the phrase statute of limitations to the statute, until the time limit itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 实务把 statute of limitations 简称为 the statute，久而久之，时限本身也带上了这个名字，这是固定规则在时间维度上的一个特例。

senses.title: The code of an institution
senses.definition: the body of rules governing an institution such as a university, a guild, or a religious order
senses.definitionCN: 管理大学、行会或修会等机构的整套规则
senses.example: The statutes of the university govern the appointment of its officers.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的章程规定其管理人员的任命。
senses.why: Any body that sets its own rules repeats the original gesture of standing a rule up, so its code is also called statutes.
senses.whyCN: 任何团体为自己立规，都在重复「把规则立起来」这个原始动作，所以它的整套规章也被称作 statutes。

intro.en: Statute comes from Latin statutum, a thing established, from statuere, to set up, which is related to stare, to stand.
intro.cn: statute 来自拉丁语 statutum（被立定之物），源于 statuere（立定、设立），并与 stare（站立）同源。

items.en: Stare means to stand, and status means a standing position.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，status 意为站立的状态或位置。

items.en: Statuere means to set something up, to fix it, or to decide it.
items.cn: statuere 意为把某物立起来、固定下来或作出决定。

items.en: Statutum, its neuter past participle, means something established, hence a decree.
items.cn: statutum 是其中性过去分词，意为被立定之物，因此指法令。

items.en: Medieval Latin uses statutum for an ordinance or a law.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 statutum 指条例或法律。

items.en: Old French statut carries the word into the language of law.
items.cn: 古法语 statut 把这个词带入法律语言。

items.en: English adopts statute in the fourteenth century for a law made by a ruler or by parliament.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 statute，指由君主或议会制定的法律。

note.en: Statute belongs to the family of statuere, and sits close to act, legislation, and ordinance in the vocabulary of law-making.
note.cn: statute 属于 statuere 词族，在立法的词汇场中与 act、legislation、ordinance 相邻。

entries.definition: a carved or cast image of a person or an animal
entries.definitionCN: 雕像（与 statute 只差一个字母；词源上与「立起」的词根相关，但义为立起的人像）

entries.definition: the legal or social standing of a person
entries.definitionCN: 地位；法律身份（与 statute 同出 stare「站立」，义为所处的位置）

entries.definition: created or required by statute
entries.definitionCN: 法定的；成文法规定的（由 statute 派生的形容词）

entries.definition: a law passed by a legislature, often used in the title of a statute
entries.definitionCN: 法令；法案（常与 statute 互换，多用于法律名称）

entries.definition: the body of enacted laws, or the process of enacting them
entries.definitionCN: 立法；法律（作集合名词，指成文法的整体或立法活动）

entries.definition: a local law made by a city or by another local authority
entries.definitionCN: 条例；地方性法规（多由市政当局制定，位阶低于 statute）

normalIntro.en: A statute is a rule stood up and fixed: statuere sets it upright, and writing keeps it standing.
normalIntro.cn: statute 是一条被立起并固定下来的规则：statuere 把它立直，文字让它一直立着。

normal.en: Statuere means to set up, and a statute is a rule set up and fixed in writing.
normal.cn: statuere 意为立起，statute 则是被立起并用文字固定下来的规则。

normal.en: Watch the look-alikes: statute is the law, statue is the image, and status is the standing.
normal.cn: 留意形近词：statute 是法律，statue 是雕像，status 是地位。

normal.en: Collocations: statute law, statute book, statute of limitations.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：成文法、法规汇编、诉讼时效法。

normal.en: Contrast common law: common law grows from cases, while statute law is enacted.
normal.cn: 对比 common law：普通法从判例中生长，成文法则由立法制定。

normal.en: Statutory is the adjective and statutorily the adverb.
normal.cn: statutory 是形容词，statutorily 是副词。

abstract.en: Picture a stone slab carved with numbered clauses, planted upright in a market square.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板刻满编号条款，直立在集市广场中央。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk reading section five of a bound volume aloud in court.
abstract.cn: 想象书记员在法庭上朗读一本合订本里的第五条。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of matching volumes standing where case reports once stood alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排相同的法律汇编，摆在本只剩判例汇编的书架上。

examples.en: The statute took effect at the start of the financial year.
examples.cn: 该法规在财政年度开始时生效。

examples.en: Courts must interpret the statute as Parliament intended.
examples.cn: 法院必须按议会的立法意图解释该成文法。

examples.en: The limitation statute barred the claim after six years.
examples.cn: 法定时效在六年后使这项索赔失去时效保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯塔图特」——斯塔图特把议会通过的条文刻在石板上，立在城门口，来往的人都要照着办。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）→ status（站立的状态）→ statuere（立定、设立）→ statutum（被立定之物，法令）→ 古法语 statut → 英语 statute，核心义「被立起来、固定下来的规则」。

sensesIntro.en: Statute begins as an enacted written law, then the instrument itself, then the whole body of enacted law, then a time limit, and finally the rules of an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: statute 先指立法机关制定的成文法律，再指法律文本本身，然后是整个制定法体系，接着是法定时效，最后是机构的整套章程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slab of fixed clauses standing upright where everyone can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻着固定条款的石板立在人人都看得见的地方。

branches.en: An enacted written law is the core sense.
branches.cn: 经立法制定的成文法律是核心义项。

branches.en: The instrument as a citable document is the second sense.
branches.cn: 可作为文本引用的法律文件是第二个义项。

branches.en: Enacted law as a body is the collective use.
branches.cn: 作为整体的制定法是集合用法。

branches.en: A time limit and an institutional code are two narrower offshoots.
branches.cn: 法定时效与机构章程是两个更窄的分支。

branches.en: The document and the body of law are the same thing seen singly and collectively.
branches.cn: 单份文本与整个体系，是同一事物被单数与集合地看待。

intro.en: Statute is built on Latin statuere, and English has statutory plus a cluster of look-alikes such as statue, status, and stature.
intro.cn: statute 建立在拉丁语 statuere 之上，英语围绕它有 statutory，以及 statue、status、stature 这一串形近词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare means to stand, status means a standing, and statuere means to set up or ordain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，status 意为站立的状态，statuere 意为立定或设立。

items.example: Stare supplies the standing image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: stare 为整个词族提供「站立」的意象。

items.example: Status is the standing that a person or a thing holds.
items.exampleCN: status 是人或物所处的位置。

items.example: Statuere turns standing into an act of setting up.
items.exampleCN: statuere 把「站立」变成「立起」的动作。

items.example: Statutum is the direct source of statute.
items.exampleCN: statutum 是 statute 的直接来源。

items.example: Statute keeps the sense of a fixed, written rule.
items.exampleCN: statute 保留了「固定的成文规则」这一含义。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms statutory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 构成 statutory。

items.example: Statutory describes what a statute requires.
items.exampleCN: statutory 描述成文法所要求的内容。

items.example: Statutorily adds the adverb suffix -ly.
items.exampleCN: statutorily 加了副词后缀 -ly。

items.example: Statue looks like statute but names an image.
items.exampleCN: statue 看起来像 statute，但指的是雕像。

items.example: Stature keeps the image of standing upright.
items.exampleCN: stature 保留了「直立」的意象。

items.meaning: to set up or make up
items.example: Constitute adds the prefix con- to statuere.
items.exampleCN: constitute 在 statuere 前加了前缀 con-。
